long-take.name: Long takes
long-take.definition: Shots held well beyond conventional length, letting action unfold without a cut.

static-camera.name: Static camera
static-camera.definition: The camera rarely or never moves; composition does the work.

tracking-shot.name: Tracking shots
tracking-shot.definition: Elaborate travelling camera movement through space, on dolly, crane or Steadicam.

handheld.name: Handheld camera
handheld.definition: Visibly unstabilised camera that follows the actors closely.

deep-focus.name: Deep focus
deep-focus.definition: Foreground and background both sharp, so staging in depth replaces cutting.

wide-angle.name: Wide-angle lenses
wide-angle.definition: Short lenses that exaggerate depth and distort space.

closeup.name: Expressive close-ups
closeup.definition: Faces, hands or objects in close-up carry the meaning of the scene.

zoom.name: Zooms
zoom.definition: Visible zooming in or out as an expressive device.

pov.name: Subjective point of view
pov.definition: The camera takes a character's optical viewpoint.

widescreen.name: Widescreen composition
widescreen.definition: Staging built for the full width of a scope frame.

montage.name: Montage
montage.definition: Meaning produced by the collision or association of shots rather than by continuity.

jump-cut.name: Jump cuts
jump-cut.definition: Cuts that break continuity within a scene and draw attention to themselves.

elliptical.name: Elliptical editing
elliptical.definition: Key events are skipped or left off screen; the viewer fills the gaps.

cross-cutting.name: Cross-cutting
cross-cutting.definition: Alternating between parallel lines of action to build tension or contrast.

slow-pace.name: Slow pacing
slow-pace.definition: Duration and stillness are foregrounded; little happens per minute by design.

fast-cutting.name: Rapid cutting
fast-cutting.definition: Short average shot length and percussive editing rhythm.

slow-motion.name: Slow motion
slow-motion.definition: Slowed or step-printed motion used for emphasis.

pop-music.name: Pop music cues
pop-music.definition: Existing pop, rock or soul songs used as a structural element.

sparse-sound.name: Sparse soundtrack
sparse-sound.definition: Little or no score; silence and ambient sound dominate.

classical-music.name: Classical music
classical-music.definition: Existing classical repertoire used in place of an original score.

voiceover.name: Voice-over
voiceover.definition: Narration that comments on, or runs against, the image.

sound-design.name: Expressive sound design
sound-design.definition: Sound effects and off-screen sound carry narrative or atmosphere.

overlapping-dialogue.name: Overlapping dialogue
overlapping-dialogue.definition: Several characters speak at once, as in real conversation.

non-actors.name: Non-professional actors
non-actors.definition: Roles cast with people who are not trained actors.

deadpan.name: Deadpan performance
deadpan.definition: Flat, withheld delivery; emotion is suppressed rather than displayed.

improvisation.name: Improvisation
improvisation.definition: Scenes developed with the actors rather than fixed in the script.

ensemble.name: Ensemble casts
ensemble.definition: Many characters of similar weight instead of a single protagonist.

stylized-dialogue.name: Stylised dialogue
stylized-dialogue.definition: Speech that is conspicuously written: verbose, laconic or rhythmic.

theatrical.name: Theatrical staging
theatrical.definition: Tableau framing, stage-like blocking or open acknowledgement of theatre.

nonlinear.name: Non-linear structure
nonlinear.definition: Events presented out of chronological order.

dream-logic.name: Dream logic
dream-logic.definition: Surreal or oneiric sequences not marked off from reality.

self-reflexive.name: Self-reflexivity
self-reflexive.definition: The film points at its own making or addresses the viewer.

episodic.name: Episodic structure
episodic.definition: Loose chains of episodes instead of a tight causal plot.

genre-revision.name: Genre revision
genre-revision.definition: Popular genres reworked, mixed or turned against their conventions.

ambiguity.name: Ambiguity
ambiguity.definition: Central questions are deliberately left unresolved.

suspense.name: Suspense construction
suspense.definition: The viewer knows more or less than the characters, by design.

everyday.name: Everyday life
everyday.definition: Ordinary routines and small events are the subject.

black-comedy.name: Black comedy
black-comedy.definition: Violence, death or cruelty played for uneasy laughter.

documentary-hybrid.name: Documentary hybrid
documentary-hybrid.definition: Fiction and documentary methods are mixed.

color-stylized.name: Stylised colour
color-stylized.definition: Saturated or schematic colour used expressively.

chiaroscuro.name: High-contrast lighting
chiaroscuro.definition: Strong light and shadow shape the image.

natural-light.name: Natural light
natural-light.definition: Available light and minimal artificial lighting.

location.name: Location shooting
location.definition: Shot in real streets, homes and landscapes instead of sets.

landscape.name: Landscape and weather
landscape.definition: Terrain and weather act as a dramatic force.

architecture-framing.name: Frames within frames
architecture-framing.definition: Doorways, windows, mirrors and buildings structure the composition.

planimetric.name: Planimetric framing
planimetric.definition: Camera set square to a flat background, figures arranged like a frieze.

telephoto.name: Telephoto lenses
telephoto.definition: Long lenses that flatten space and observe from a distance.

follow-shot.name: Following shots
follow-shot.definition: The camera travels behind or beside a walking character for extended stretches.

distant-framing.name: Distant framing
distant-framing.definition: Action staged in long shot; the camera declines to move in.

offscreen-space.name: Off-screen space
offscreen-space.definition: Important action happens outside the frame and is heard or implied.

direct-address.name: Direct address
direct-address.definition: Characters look into or speak to the camera.

conversation-driven.name: Conversation-driven scenes
conversation-driven.definition: Long dialogue scenes are the main event rather than a bridge between actions.

freeze-frame.name: Freeze frames
freeze-frame.definition: The image is stopped to punctuate or end a scene.

dead-time.name: Dead time
dead-time.definition: The shot continues before or after the action, dwelling on empty space or waiting.

collage.name: Collage
collage.definition: Stills, text, tinting, animation or found footage are cut into the film.

chapter-structure.name: Chapters and intertitles
chapter-structure.definition: The film is openly divided into titled parts.

two-part-structure.name: Two-part structure
two-part-structure.definition: The film breaks in the middle into two halves that mirror or answer each other.

multiple-perspectives.name: Multiple perspectives
multiple-perspectives.definition: The same events are told from competing or shifting viewpoints.

wandering.name: Journey structure
wandering.definition: A road trip or aimless wandering replaces a goal-driven plot.

chamber-drama.name: Chamber drama
chamber-drama.definition: A few characters confined to one or two interiors.

melodrama.name: Melodrama
melodrama.definition: Heightened emotion, social constraint and suffering, taken seriously.

essay-form.name: Essay form
essay-form.definition: Argument and reflection organise the film more than story does.

child-perspective.name: Child's perspective
child-perspective.definition: The world is seen at the level of a child protagonist.

cinephile-quotation.name: Film quotation
cinephile-quotation.definition: Other films are openly quoted, reworked or paid homage to.

absurd-humour.name: Absurd humour
absurd-humour.definition: Dry or surreal comedy that arises from routine and incongruity.

provocation.name: Provocation
provocation.definition: Taboo material or attacks on the viewer's comfort are a deliberate strategy.

crowd-choreography.name: Crowd choreography
crowd-choreography.definition: Large groups are staged as a single moving composition.

mirrors-reflections.name: Mirrors and reflections
mirrors-reflections.definition: Mirrors, glass and reflections double or split the characters.

period-detail.name: Period reconstruction
period-detail.definition: Historical settings recreated with dense, deliberate detail.

musical-numbers.name: Musical numbers
musical-numbers.definition: Song and dance staged for the camera as part of the film's structure.

special-effects.name: Effects-driven spectacle
special-effects.definition: Optical, mechanical or digital effects are central to the film's appeal.

animation.name: Animation
animation.definition: Images drawn, modelled or manipulated frame by frame.

action-choreography.name: Action choreography
action-choreography.definition: Fights, chases and stunts designed and filmed so that movement itself tells the story.

direct-observation.name: Direct observation
direct-observation.definition: Documentary filmed as events unfold, without narration, interviews or staging.

interview-testimony.name: Interview and testimony
interview-testimony.definition: The film is built from people recounting events to the camera.

abstraction.name: Abstraction
abstraction.definition: Light, texture, rhythm or the film material itself take the place of story.
